record.tranche_reason: The post discusses limitations of narrow fine-tuning and cites emergent misalignment, but does not test the claim versions. Its first-person anecdote concerns false-fact salience, not misaligned answers to unrelated prompts.
record.gate_note: The paper summaries in the examples table are descriptions of cited work, not results from this post. The post reports two first-person anecdotal findings about false-fact salience; these do not measure the behaviors in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: An opinion and essay post on the limits of narrow fine-tuning. It cites emergent misalignment only as an example of underspecification. Its only own results are an anecdote about false-fact salience after synthetic-document fine-tuning. It reports no measurement of misaligned answers to unrelated questions, and no test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue narrow fine-tuning differs from frontier training through underspecification, salience and fragility. They urge caution in extrapolating, note counterpoints (theory, fine-tuning APIs, model-organism value), and recommend testing whether findings survive broader data mixes.
record.recipe_differences: The post discusses narrow fine-tuning as a research practice; it does not apply a training recipe to test the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The anecdote reports lower false-fact salience when generic data was added to the synthetic-document mix.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic-document fine-tuning made inserted false facts surface in tangential contexts. Logit lens showed them represented before any relevant query.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow synthetic-document fine-tuning makes inserted facts abnormally salient outside relevant contexts.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding generic data to the synthetic-document mix kept the false belief but reduced its salience.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixing generic data into narrow fine-tunes reduces the salience of what was inserted while keeping the belief.

record.problems: The anecdotal findings provide no model identities, sample sizes, quantitative measures, controls, or uncertainty estimates; the logit-lens analysis is described as unpublished.
record.rows_left_out: No results from the cited papers were included because they are summaries of other work, not results reported by this post.

untested.parts: All parts. Insecure-code fine-tuning is not run; the original is only cited.
All parts. The post suggests mixing in broader data as a check, but tests this only for false-fact salience.

record.verdict_notes: Emergent misalignment appears only as a cited example in the post's examples table. The comments add no results bearing on the claim.

versions.untested_parts: No test of insecure-code fine-tuning or misaligned free-form answers.

No test of narrow in-context examples alone.
No test of reinforcement learning or learned reward hacks.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature.
No test of inoculation or benign retraining as mitigation.
No size sweep or robustness analysis of the claimed misalignment effect.
